title: Fit a replacement helmet visor
instruction: Fit the visor onto both hinge catches. Close it fully, reopen it, then let go with both catches still secure.
context: Replacing a worn visor requires aligning two spaced hinge catches and checking that the fitted shield opens and closes.
setup: An inert full-size helmet shell (290 × 236 × 250 mm) is secured to a 220 mm display base on a 747.5 mm-high table. Its centre is at (220, 0, 135) mm above the table. The helmet starts without a visor, with hinge bases 264 mm apart; each base has a 10 × 14 mm downward spring-release button with 4 mm travel. A 2 mm curved polycarbonate replacement visor rests at (170, −300) mm. The fixed layout and generic catch geometry are supplied in geometry.py. Both arms use 40 × 10 × 1 mm replacement precision fingers with silicone contact faces and 6 N jaw effort.
scoring: Broken parts score zero. Otherwise award the highest applicable score: 0.25 for one engaged catch; 0.5 for both; 0.75 for closing the attached visor to within 8° of shut. Full score also requires reopening it by at least 55° and releasing both hands for two seconds with both catches still engaged. Other outcomes score zero. Check retention and travel in the video using a simple angle template.
fidelity: The visor has a rigid curved centre and compliant end ears. Spring trigger movement releases the native hinge constraints. Local hook seating is approximated by capture within 2.5 mm and 6 degrees at low speed; no object pose is written. This is a generic two-catch quick-release design, not a certified replacement part. The helmet is inert and not worn by a person.
scores: Development only: not validated; do not submit.
reset_notes: Release both catches, remove the visor and restore its pictured pose. Replace damaged components. The helmet begins bare: removing the old visor is outside this task. Use an inert display assembly, never protective equipment worn by a person.
